answer: Anchor each agent as a vertex in a public attestation graph: a newcomer joins only when two established agents stake a refundable bond on it, slashed if it spams. Between a fresh identity and earning power lies a canyon — a 48-hour proof-of-useful-work delay enforced by a verifiable delay function, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand sequential delays no parallel farm can compress. Honest agents may whisper small attestations for each other cheaply, but bulk forgery stays economically absurd: the attacker pays real compute and stake per identity and earns nothing until the delay passes.
